newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DALGLISH SAYS HE COULD NOT REFUSE NEWCASTLE JOB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DALGLISH SAYS HE COULD NOT REFUSE NEWCASTLE JOB.

text.p: Kenny Dalglish, named as Newcastle United's new manager on Tuesday said his aim for the club was to bring it long-overdue success -- but would not commit himself to bringing the title back to St James' Park this season.
Speaking at a hastily-arranged news conference to announce his appointment, Dalglish was asked whether the title was a realistic target for this season.

"If you set targets and you don't reach them that can be seen as a failure," said the man who has succeeded Kevin Keegan who left Newcastle six days ago. Then, smiling broadly, he added: "But we've got a much better chance than many other teams."

"I couldn't refuse the job," he said. "I'm really looking forward to it, Newcastle are a huge club. Kevin did a superb job in the five years he was here and it is not the kind of job that comes along every day. Kevin has left a great foundation for me to build on."

Newcastle chairman Sir John Hall, who was believed to favour Bobby Robson over Dalglish, warmly welcomed Dalglish and said: "I would like to place on record my thanks and my board's sincere thanks to Kevin Keegan for five wonderful years.

"To move forward to the new millennium we need a new manager to take us there and I am delighted to welcome Kenny Dalglish. I am certain with his record he will do wonders at this club, a club with great expectations."

Dalglish has reportedly signed a three-and-a-half year contract with the Magpies who play their first match since his arrival against first division Charlton Athletic in an F.A. Cup third round replay at St James' Park on Wednesday.
